subject.title: fix(agents): repair double-escaped JSON strings in tool call argument…

question: Should this runtime accept a lossy all-provider content heuristic, or must repair be limited to a decoding boundary that can distinguish malformed double encoding from intentional literal escapes?
rationale: After JSON parsing, the affected string no longer carries provenance that distinguishes accidental double escaping from intentional literal escape text, so the acceptable compatibility contract requires maintainer judgment.

options.title: Require provenance-based repair
options.body: Do not merge the unconditional heuristic; repair only where raw tool-call decoding proves a double-encoded representation, with positive and literal-preservation regression coverage.

options.title: Accept the heuristic risk
options.body: Merge the all-provider rewrite and explicitly accept that some intentionally literal structural escape sequences may be converted at runtime.

recommendation.title: Require provenance-based repair
recommendation.body: Do not merge the unconditional heuristic; repair only where raw tool-call decoding proves a double-encoded representation, with positive and literal-preservation regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The choice changes embedded-agent runtime compatibility rather than being a narrow test-only correction.
